reasons: F01, F02, F15: material weakness tied to staffing/segregation of duties, with an interim or acting CFO, points to a thin finance function and weak controls over the close.
F03: no auditor ICFR attestation, so the control weakness has not been tested independently.
F04, F19, F21, R16: going-concern doubt, a covenant breach/waiver/amendment and a dependence on raising capital give management strong pressure to present better results.
F11: material related-party transactions add risk of non-arm's-length or poorly disclosed dealings.

R02, R15: gross margin index of 0.58 (a sharp margin improvement) and a large ROA improvement (+0.24) despite sales falling (R04 0.94) are unusual for a distressed company and need scrutiny (e.g. cost classification or reserve releases).
R03, R13, F24: asset quality index of 1.7 and a soft-assets share of 0.95, plus a CAM on goodwill/intangibles, mean a balance sheet dominated by judgmental assets with impairment risk.
F28: segment/reporting change reduces comparability year over year.

R08, R09, R10, R11, R18, R01, R17: accruals are strongly negative, receivables fell sharply relative to sales, the Beneish M-score (-4.19) is well below threshold and the F-score (0.51) is low, so there is no accrual-based sign of earnings inflation. This offsets part of the qualitative risk.
R19: operating cash flow to net income of -54.74 shows that earnings and cash flow diverge, likely because net income is near zero; this is noisy but worth reconciling.
